**Study reference:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning*, §10.3. The examples, reasoning and notation explanations are written independently.

## Start from a problem

The same PCA direction can be derived by minimising reconstruction error. This makes the compression cost explicit in the original feature space.

## Formulate the problem mathematically

$$
\min_{W^\top W=I_k}\sum_{i=1}^N\|\boldsymbol x_i-\boldsymbol\mu-WW^\top(\boldsymbol x_i-\boldsymbol\mu)\|_2^2
$$

This relation identifies the required structure. Interpret the symbols using the stated model rather than memorising the formula without its assumptions.

## Derive a worked result

Project x=(3,1) onto the unit diagonal direction w=(1,1)/sqrt(2). The score is 4/sqrt(2), and reconstruction is (2,2). The residual is (1,-1) and squared reconstruction error equals 2.

## Why the mathematics matters

For centered Euclidean data, maximising projected variance and minimising reconstruction error choose the same principal subspace. This equality relies on orthogonal projections and a consistent metric.

## Explain or calculate

Why is reconstruction along a unit direction WW^T x rather than simply W^T x?
